Q: How to install nvm in windows A:

If you got here in 2026, the official NVM repository now supports Windows.

All you have to do is using cURL in Git Bash. Run the command below:

curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.40.4/install.sh | bash

After that, create the file ~/.bashrc with the following content:

export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"

[ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" # This loads nvm

Then you reopen the terminal or type source ~/.bashrc and that's it! It should work properly using Git Bash.

Q: Automatic regactoring C++ code to pairs of header-source files A:

Functions can be declared in any order in the header. Any classes are also defined in the header; note that the definition of a class isn't the same as definitions of its members.

When those same functions are defined in source, they already know that everything declared in the header will exist so you can already use all of it - call both your functions from their bodies, use your classes etc.

That's part of why header-source separation is good, you don't need to worry about order. First you declare what you're implementing, then you include the header in source, then you define what you declared. You should read up more on headers vs sources, declarations, definitions and associated topics like ODR, inline, the (non-)handling of undefined references etc. It works very well as designed so I'm sure you're missing something simple. Unfortunately it's hard to tell exactly what.

Once you've got the design down properly, use an IDE - those are the tools for fixing your code automatically.

Q: How to exit on a found string for aws logs tail A:

aws logs ... |Where { $_ -match 'term' } |Select -First 1
